glosses: gerund of verwahrlosen
to become neglected
оставлять без присмотра, запускать
прийти в состояние запущенности (в беспорядок)
остаться без присмотра
zaniedbywać, zaniedbać, zostawiać na pastwę losu, zostawić na pastwę losu
intransitiv, Hilfsverb sein:
in einen von fortschreitendem Verfall und zunehmendem Mangel an Sauberkeit und Ordnung gekennzeichneten oder sonst allgemein schlechten Zustand geraten

examples.text: Schon vor vielen Jahren hat diese Gegend hier angefangen, immer mehr zu verwahrlosen.
Das Jugendamt entfernte vier Kinder aus der immer mehr verwahrlosenden Wohnung ihrer Eltern.
Es hat sich niemand um Opa gekümmert und deswegen war er bei seinem Tod völlig verwahrlost.
Diese Wohnung ist vollkommen verwahrlost.
Die Eltern meiner Klassenkameradin verwahrlosen immer mehr.
Du bist sittlich absolut verwahrlost.
Es machte uns alle furchtbar traurig, dass du immer mehr verwahrlostest.

glosses: transitiv, Hilfsverb haben:
entgegen einer Verpflichtung so schlecht für jemanden oder etwas sorgen, dass dieser oder dieses einen Schaden erleidet oder einen solchen anrichten kann

examples.text: Du hast deine Kinder verwahrlost.
Weh dir, wenn du das Feuer verwahrlost und es unser Heim verbrennt.
Ich werde meinen Sohn nicht verwahrlosen.

glosses: etwas unsorgfältig, unsachgemäß oder unrichtig ausführen oder betreiben

examples.text: Du hast deinen Dienst die ganze Zeit verwahrlost.

glosses: etwas kaum beachten, es gering schätzen; es versäumen, sich etwas nutzbar zu machen

examples.text: All die Dienste, die ich dir erwiesen habe, hast du stets verwahrlost.
Die Gelegenheiten, die das Leben meinem Onkel gewährte, verwahrloste er ausnahmslos.

glosses: eine nachteilige Entwicklung durch Nachlässigkeit unbemerkt eintreten lassen

examples.text: Während Rickmer im Watt umherspazierte, verwahrloste er, dass die Flut kam.

glosses: jemanden oder etwas schädigen, verderben oder gefährden

examples.text: Ihr habt eure Gesundheit durch das viele Rauchen verwahrlost.

glosses: reflexiv:
sich selbst mutwillig gefährden

examples.text: Ich bin nicht so dumm, dass ich mich verwahrloste, indem ich mich mit der Syphilis ansteckte.

glosses: Having deteriorated, degraded or fallen from normal, coherent, balanced and desirable to undesirable and typically abnormal.
Having lost good or desirable qualities; hence also having bad character or habits, base, immoral, corrupt.

examples.text: faint-hearted and degenerate king

But what can Cato do
Againſt a World, a baſe degenerate World,
That courts the Yoke, and bows the Neck to Cæſar?
As you grew more degenerate and base, I sent you millions of the croaking race
If my boy is not tempted to gamble at a fashionable card party he will never learn from the degenerate, blackleg gamblers in the joint.

The author explores the gap between the degenerate, elitist society of the domes and the working population. He criticizes the world of luxury and ease that easily ignores the sufferings of the majority.
What are the odds that an alcoholic and degenerate gambler with no money management skills could survive in a city that ate addicts for lunch and dreams for dinner?

glosses: Having lost functionality in general.

examples.text: It is likely that the long evolutionary trajectory of Mycoplasma went from a reductive autotroph to oxidative heterotroph to a cell-wall–defective degenerate parasite. This evolutionary trajectory assumes the simplicity to complexity route of biogenesis, a point of view that is not universally accepted.

glosses: Having multiple domain elements correspond to one element of the range.

examples.text: The genetic code is degenerate because a single amino acid can be coded by one of several codons.

glosses: Qualitatively different, usually simpler, than typical objects of its class.

examples.text: A degenerate circle, having radius zero, consists of a single point.
We now apply the geometrical construction explained in the appendix to the degenerate triangle ABC.

glosses: Having multiple different (linearly independent) eigenvectors.
Having the same quantum energy level.
One who is degenerate, who has fallen from previous stature; an immoral or corrupt person.

examples.text: In the cult of degenerates, acts of decency, kindness and modesty could be seen as acts of apostasy.
The undeveloped or mysterically confused thought which exists in savages is fully exemplified in the childish or crazy atavistic anthropomorphism and symbolism so prevalent among degenerates.

glosses: To lose good or desirable qualities.

examples.text: His condition continued to degenerate even after admission to hospital.

Another bird quickly learned to imitate the song of a canary that was mated with it, but as the parrakeet improved in the performance the canary degenerated, and came at last to mingle the other bird's harsh chitterings with its own proper music.
The haploid ovum is now called an ootid (Fig. 8—7). The second polar body degenerates, sometimes dividing before it dies.

Cumaratunga was so furious that he intensified his campaign for revitalizing the traditional practices of asweddumization, so that neglected arable land could be rehabilitated, and a degenerating economy restructured and rejuvenated.

glosses: To cause to lose good or desirable qualities.

To fail to care for or attend to something.

examples.text: to neglect duty or business;  to neglect to pay debts

I hope
 My absence doth neglect no great designs.

This, my long sufferance and my day of grace,
 Those who neglect and scorn, shall never taste.

One of the hidden glories of Victorian engineering is proper drains.[…]But out of sight is out of mind. And that, together with the inherent yuckiness of the subject, means that many old sewers have been neglected and are in dire need of repair.

glosses: To omit to notice; to forbear to treat with attention or respect; to slight.

examples.text: to neglect strangers

glosses: To fail to do or carry out something due to oversight or carelessness.

examples.text: A friend of mine who runs an intellectual magazine was grousing about his movie critic, complaining that though the fellow had liked The Godfather (page 58), he had neglected to label it clearly as a masterpiece.

glosses: To ignore for the sake of simplifying calculations without significantly affecting accuracy.

examples.text: We can neglect this term, as it approaches zero in the limit anyway.
This problem says to neglect air resistance.

glosses: The act of neglecting.
The state of being neglected.
Habitual lack of care.

examples.text: Fifteen participants argued that the neglect of discourse on relationships had major implications for the ability of adolescents to acquire courtship skills and maintain relationships. This neglect means that the students acquire knowledge and skills through the media and by observing and imitating others in their immediate environment.
